title: Data Handling and Probability
summary: Collecting and grouping data, averages as balance points, choosing (and questioning) charts, and chance: dice experiments, sample spaces and probability.

ib.statementOfInquiry: Representing data and reasoning about chance help us make fair, justified decisions and spot misleading claims.

factual: How do we find the mean, median, mode and range?
How do we draw a pie chart?
How do we calculate a probability?
conceptual: Why can the mean and median tell different stories?
Why do experimental results get closer to theory with more trials?
debatable: Are games of chance ever truly fair?
